newsitem.title: DUBAI: Proposed offset projects in UAE worth $6 billion.
newsitem.headline: Proposed offset projects in UAE worth $6 billion.

text.p: Projects proposed under the United Arab Emirates' offset programme are worth 22 billion dirhams ($6 billion), an official said in remarks published on Sunday.
But Mohammad al-Mazroui, UAE Offset Group deputy director, told the London-based Asharq al-Awsat newspaper that projects worth only 1 billion dirhams had been implemented so far.

The UAE is a big buyer in the international arms market, luring weapons makers seeking billions of dollars in sales while stipulating they offset some of the contract value by investing it in locally.

Some of the companies say they are frustrated with the mandatory offset programme that the UAE hopes will diversify its economy and attract capital. Weapons manufacturers complain of limited investment opportunities in the oil-dominated economy.

"We agree that there is difficulty in finding appropriate investment opportunities...not because of the lack of investment opportunities" but because implementing the offset programme in the UAE differed from offset schemes in other world countries," Mazroui said.
Weapons manufacturers say the UAE's offset requirements were too demanding.

They cite one stipulation that defence companies are required to invest in commercially sound projects with local investors in 49/51 percent joint ventures that generate added value to the UAE over a period of seven years equivalent to 60 percent of the value of the sales contract.
Offset ventures, which exclude the oil sector, include a solar power firm, a medical diagnostic centre and a company that leases industrial equipment.
